title: The localization of a ring at a minimal prime has nilpotent maximal ideal; a field if the ring is reduced
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a minimal prime ideal (a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal). Then every element of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ of the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is nilpotent (equivalently, $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is the only prime ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$). If moreover $R$ is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements), then $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}=0$ and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field.
